lead: Pembroke Pines plumbing deals with heat, heavy rain, slab homes and fast 1980s and 1990s growth. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Pembroke Pines.
risk: slab leaks, cast-iron drain failures and polybutylene pipe
risk_short: slab leaks, old drains and old pipes
why: Eastern Pembroke Pines has homes from the 1960s and 1970s with cast-iron drains under the slab. Much of the west was built in the 1980s and 1990s, and some of those homes have polybutylene pipe.
Summer storms and hurricanes flood low streets and back up drains. Many homes are in communities with HOA rules for exterior work.
water: Pembroke Pines pumps water from the Biscayne Aquifer and treats it at the city's plant. It is moderately hard.
tips: Look for gray pipe stamped PB2110.
Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Check HOA rules before exterior work.
areas: PipeMend works in Pembroke Lakes, Chapel Trail, Silver Lakes, Pembroke Falls, Pembroke Shores, Grand Palms and every other Pembroke Pines neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Pembroke Pines Building Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Do Pembroke Pines homes have polybutylene pipe?
faq.a: Some homes built in the 1980s and early 1990s do. Look for gray plastic pipe stamped PB2110. Many insurers ask about it, and replacing it prevents sudden leaks.
